hero.title: Your first wave and your first ceviche. Same day.
hero.tagline: Two hours in the water with Diego. An afternoon in the kitchen with whatever the boats brought in. Dinner on the sand while the sun drops behind the point.
hero.imageAlt: Diego preparing ceviche on the beach at sunset

intro.heading: Most surf trips give you one skill. This one gives you two.
intro.body: You can book a lesson anywhere. What you cannot book anywhere is the walk to the pier afterwards, picking the fish that decides dinner, and learning to cut it properly from someone who cooks for a living. You go home able to catch a wave and make a ceviche — and knowing why Peruvians argue about both.

surf.title: Surf with Diego
surf.body: Two hours in the water. Four people at most, so every wave you miss gets explained. Board and wetsuit are on us.

cook.title: Cook it yourself
cook.body: Lime, ají limo, red onion, fish that was swimming this morning. Diego does not demonstrate while you watch — you hold the knife.
cook.imageAlt: Hands preparing ceviche on a wooden table

eat.title: Eat what you made
eat.body: One long table, everything you cooked, and the light going orange over the point. A Pisco Sour if you want one.
eat.imageAlt: Guests at a long table at sunset

groups.title: Four people maximum
groups.body: Small enough that Diego is watching you specifically, not the group.

gear.title: Board and wetsuit
gear.body: Included. The Humboldt current runs colder than the latitude suggests — bring nothing.

photos.title: Your photos, free
photos.body: Someone shoots while you surf. You get the files afterwards. Nobody tries to sell them back to you.

food.title: Ingredients and dinner
food.body: Everything you cook and everything you drink is part of the day, not an extra.

place.heading: A left that runs for 300 metres, in a town most people drive past
place.body: Lobitos sits where the Sechura desert meets the Pacific. It was a British oil town once, and the wooden houses they raised on stilts are still standing — sun-bleached, leaning, lived in. Between them, shipping containers have become kitchens and rooms. There is no strip, no resort and no queue: sand, wind, one of the most consistent left-hand point breaks on the continent, and people who came for a season and never left.

kitchenTeaser.heading: Nothing here came out of a freezer
kitchenTeaser.body: Coastal Peruvian cooking is fish, lime, chilli and knowing when to stop. You will learn all four.

hero.title: Surf
hero.tagline: Lobitos breaks left, long and predictable. A forgiving place to start, and a hard place to stop improving.

levels.heading: Tell us where you are, not where you wish you were

beginner.title: Never stood up
beginner.body: We start inside, where the wave has already broken and there is white water to spare. Paddling, position, pop-up. Most people ride something on the first morning. Almost everyone does by the second.

intermediate.title: Standing, but the wave decides
intermediate.body: You get to your feet and then go wherever the foam sends you. We work on reading the section, angling the take-off, and staying ahead of the break instead of behind it.

advanced.title: You do not need a lesson
advanced.body: You need someone who knows which bank works on which tide, and why yesterday was better. Diego surfs with you and talks between sets.

practical.heading: The things people email to ask

season.title: When should I come?
season.body: Lobitos works every month of the year. April to October brings the bigger, longer swells. December to March is warmer, smaller and far kinder if you are learning.

water.title: Is the water cold?
water.body: Colder than a map suggests — the Humboldt current runs up this coast from Antarctica. A shorty is usually enough, a full suit is better in winter. Both are included, so bring neither.

safety.title: What if I get into trouble?
safety.body: You will not be alone in the water at any point. Small groups, a briefing before you go in, and spots chosen for you rather than for the photograph. Lobitos has rocks and current in places, and we simply do not take you there.

imageAlts.wave: Surfer riding along an open face

hero.title: Kitchen
hero.tagline: The Peruvian coast eats raw fish cured in lime, with chilli and sweet potato. Everything else is a variation on that.

intro.heading: There is no menu, because there is no fixed catch
intro.body: We walk down to the boats, look at what came in, and build the afternoon around it. That is not a limitation — it is the entire reason it tastes like this. What follows is what usually turns up, not a promise.

ceviche.name: Ceviche clásico
ceviche.note: Fish, lime, red onion, ají limo, sweet potato

lomo.name: Lomo saltado
lomo.note: Beef, onion, tomato, soy — Peru's Chinese inheritance

tiradito.name: Tiradito de ají amarillo
tiradito.note: Sliced thin, yellow chilli cream, no onion

causa.name: Causa limeña
causa.note: Cold potato layered with lime, chilli and avocado

parrillada.name: Parrillada de mariscos
parrillada.note: Whatever the grill can take, garlic and lime

conchas.name: Conchas a la parmesana
conchas.note: Scallops in the shell, butter, cheese, grill

pisco.name: Pisco sour
pisco.note: Pisco, lime, syrup, egg white, bitters

kitchen.diet: Vegetarian and vegan versions of nearly all of this are straightforward. Tell us when you write and we shop differently — decide on the day and you get whatever the boats had.

hero.title: Stay
hero.tagline: Wood, corrugated iron and shipping containers, in the one town where all three make sense.

intro.heading: Close enough to hear whether it is working
intro.body: Lobitos was built twice. First by an oil company that raised wooden houses on stilts a century ago, then by surfers who arrived later and built with what was lying around — mostly containers, mostly better than you would expect. Rooms are simple and the wifi is slow. The wall between you and the Pacific is thin enough that you will know the swell size before you open your eyes.

stay.note: There are only a few rooms and they are not always free. Ask when you write: we will tell you what is open, or send you to neighbours we would stay with ourselves.

hero.title: Diego
hero.tagline: Surfer and cook — which is why you do not have to choose.

about.body1: Diego grew up on this coast and has spent most of his life between the water and a kitchen. He teaches the way people teach when they are not in a hurry: fewer instructions, more time in the water, and a habit of pointing at things until you see them too.
about.body2: The cooking half was an accident. Guests kept staying for dinner, then kept asking how it was made, and at some point the second half of the day stopped being something that just happened and became the reason people book.
